## Claims
- [source-backed] RWY Theorem 4.8 works integrally in \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) and gives the two Schur generating families for \(J_v\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]
- [source-backed] RWY’s proof uses vertical-strip Pieri identities and degree inductions; the supplied passage gives no Smith-form, determinantal-divisor, or unimodular-minor statement. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 1005-1041; 1068-1142]
- [source-backed] St. Dizier–Yong prove lower-adjoined-family minimality for \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), under \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [source-backed] Their proof reduces Littlewood–Richardson syzygies to tall/wide linear equations and a coproduct-tensor algorithm, rather than stating a degreewise Pieri-matrix Smith-form or unimodular-complement theorem. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 254-261; 494-516; 790-831]

## Strategy
The supplied external-search record contains only `persisted:source-29,source-39,source-30`, yielding the already-known RWY (2011) and St. Dizier–Yong (2024) works (with duplicate renderings of the latter). It contains no recorded targeted query for “Smith form,” “determinantal divisor,” “unimodular minor,” or “Pieri matrix.”

Compared with the current integral interval/Pieri-matrix objects, RWY concerns the same integral \(J_v\) and supplies Pieri elimination for generation; St. Dizier–Yong concerns the same Grassmannian quotient and proves lower-family minimality via LR/Hopf methods. Neither supplied theorem supplies the requested matrix/SNF certificate.

## Gaps
The requested target is **not established**: no targeted external-literature/arXiv search for the four specified matrix terms was executed or supplied. The negative conclusion is bounded to the two inspected works and does not exclude relevant literature elsewhere.
